design.chosen: the shared crate aprender-mcp-decide-lambda becomes a model-agnostic library carrying the bootstrap runtime (bootstrap::run(package)); each served model gets a THIN <server>-lambda crate (Cargo.toml, a shim main.rs, README) that cargo-pmcp's resolver finds first; the server id is a required argument of the six AWS-touching recipes and _laya-server-check refuses an id with no thin crate

rejected.rename_in_place: renaming aprender-mcp-decide-lambda to the new id would bind the shared runtime to one model and break the next model's name
rejected.keep_both_bins: two bootstrap bins in two crates grows the FALSIFY-MONO-011 register 9 -> 10 (a human gate) and leaves the old id resolvable by the resolver as a trap
rejected.symlinked_crate_dir: a symlinked crate directory is a second path to the same package; cargo metadata, git and the resolver disagree about it
rejected.bin_path_outside_package: a [[bin]] path pointing outside the package is refused or fragile across cargo versions and hides the real source from the package
rejected.per_model_deploy_root_under_crates: a deploy root per model under crates/ duplicates the .pmcp/ and deploy/ state the setfit training server already owns at the shared root

priced.re_upload: reuses the existing just laya-upload, which already takes the server id and whose refusals have offline proof; costs one laya-verify pass and one 846,220,868-byte transfer (plan 10-08 measured the whole upload step at 1473 s; the split between verify and transfer is unmeasured)
priced.server_side_copy: saves the transfer and the verify pass but needs a NEW AWS-writing recipe with its own refusals and offline proof, so it adds unproven code to the path that writes to AWS

design.deploy_concurrency_limit: servers SERVE in parallel but DEPLOYS run one at a time: the shared crates root's .pmcp/ and deploy/ belong to the setfit training server and _laya-crates-root-swap installs one config alone; it refuses while a leftover backup exists, so a second concurrent deploy fails closed

findings.title: laya-deploy's first edge /health check can 404 on a brand-new server id and contain the function before the edge has registered it
findings.evidence: attempt 1: 404 at the recipe's single GET, then CONTAINED; the same GET returned 200 about 8 minutes later
findings.suggested_fix: NOT implemented: a bounded retry/wait on the edge /health check (404 only, e.g. up to 10 tries 15 s apart) before contain(); every other failure keeps containing at once. To be decided by the coordinator/owner.

findings.title: after the containment, the pmcp.run edge answers every MCP POST with 503 `Server is in error state` even though the function is un-contained and /health is 200
findings.evidence: 9 probe tries over about 3 min at 00:38Z; consistent with D-ITEM-08-17-D (sticky edge error state `/health` cannot see), here probably set by pmcp.run's own post-deploy invocation or the probes landing while the function was throttled. The edge's recovery time is undocumented
findings.status: resolved by a redeploy, not by waiting
findings.resolution: 503 `Server is in error state` observed 00:38Z-00:42Z (9 executor probe tries, about 3 min, plus later reads) with the function un-contained and /health 200; after the owner's deploy-only rerun (rc 0, 00:51-00:53Z) POST initialize returned 200 at 01:08Z and the identity probe passed first try at 01:09Z. Waiting about 3 min did not clear it; whether longer waiting would is unknown
